# 4-Week Wellness Reset for Better Sleep, Fewer Headaches, and More Daily Movement

A practical, low-cost plan built around sleep consistency, hydration, gentle movement, and screen breaks. It’s designed for mild seasonal allergies, occasional tension headaches, and a desk-based routine.

## 4-Week Routine Plan

| Week | Sleep Focus | Movement Focus | Hydration Target | Screen-Time Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixed wake time daily; bedtime within a 60-minute window | 10-minute walk after 1 meal + 2 movement breaks at work | 2.0–2.5 L/day | No screens 30 minutes before bed; 5-minute break each hour |
| 2 | Add a 20–30 minute wind-down routine | 15-minute walk 5 days/week + 5-minute mobility daily | 2.2–2.7 L/day | Same bedtime rule; reduce leisure scrolling by 15 minutes/day |
| 3 | Keep wake time stable on weekends | 20-minute brisk walk 5 days/week + 2 short strength sessions | 2.3–2.8 L/day | 10-minute break from screens every 2 hours outside work |
| 4 | Protect sleep window; aim for 7–9 hours | 25–30 minutes of activity most days + posture resets | 2.3–3.0 L/day, more on hot/allergy-heavy days | Keep bedroom screen-free; use “last check” cutoff 1 hour before bed |

## Daily Plan You Can Repeat

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clock.svg

- Morning: Get 5–10 minutes of outdoor light soon after waking; this helps anchor sleep and may reduce grogginess.
- Workday: Stand up or walk 2–3 minutes every hour; do 5 shoulder rolls, 5 chin tucks, and 5 gentle neck turns each side.
- Midday: Take a 10–20 minute walk, ideally after lunch.
- Evening: Finish caffeine 8 hours before bed; dim lights and avoid intense screen use in the last 30–60 minutes.
- Bedtime: Keep the room cool, dark, and quiet; use allergy control steps if congestion is affecting sleep.

## Headache-Prevention Habits That Fit a Desk Job

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

- Hydrate early: 1 glass of water on waking, then sip regularly through the day.
- Don’t skip meals: Long gaps can trigger tension or dehydration-related headaches.
- Check posture: Keep screen at eye level, shoulders relaxed, feet flat, and elbows supported.
- Reduce eye strain: Follow the 20-20-20 rule when possible; every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
- Loosen the neck/jaw: Unclench your jaw and drop shoulders during stressful tasks.
- Track triggers: Note sleep loss, skipped water, long screen sessions, and allergy flare-ups.

## Allergy-Friendly Sleep Support

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg

- Shower or rinse hair before bed during high-pollen days.
- Keep windows closed if pollen is high and use a fan or air circulation instead.
- Change clothes after outdoor time to reduce pollen on bedding.
- If you use allergy medicine, take it exactly as directed on the label or by your clinician.
- If congestion is disrupting sleep most nights, that’s worth discussing with a clinician.

## When to Seek Medical Care

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

See a clinician soon if you notice any of these:
- Headaches that are getting more frequent, more severe, or changing in pattern.
- Headaches with fever, neck stiffness, confusion, fainting, weakness, numbness, vision changes, or trouble speaking.
- Headaches that wake you from sleep repeatedly or happen after a head injury.
- Snoring, gasping, or unrefreshing sleep most nights.
- Persistent fatigue, mood changes, or trouble concentrating despite regular sleep.
- Seasonal allergy symptoms that are not controlled with standard measures.
- Chest pain, shortness of breath, or exercise intolerance.
